steps.say: To compare decimals, line up the decimal points. Then compare the digits from the left.

head: Ones
Tenths
Hundredths
figure.alt: A place value chart with 3.45 above 3.50, lined up by place.

steps.say: The ones are the same, so look at the tenths. 5 tenths is more than 4 tenths.
A decimal with more digits can still be the smaller number. Write a zero in the gap so both have the same number of places.
On a number line, the bigger number is further to the right.

figure.alt: A number line from 3.4 to 3.6 with 3.45 and 3.5 marked. 3.5 is further right.

steps.say: To order a list, compare the ones first, then the tenths, then the hundredths.

hints: Write each number with two decimal places, like 0.40.
check.explanation: 0.8 has 8 tenths, more than any of the other numbers, so 0.8 is the greatest.

options.why: 0.09 has 0 tenths, so it is the smallest.

check.prompt: Which list is in order from smallest to largest?
hints: Compare the tenths, then the hundredths.

options.why: This list goes from largest to smallest.
Compare the tenths first. 2.3 and 2.35 have only 3 tenths.
2.35 has 3 tenths, so it comes before 2.5.

check.prompt: Write the sign <, > or = to make this true. 4.06 ___ 4.6
hints: 4.06 has 0 tenths. How many tenths does 4.6 have?
check.explanation: 4.06 has 0 tenths and 4.6 has 6 tenths, so 4.06 < 4.6.
